newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dlr motors on and up, Eurobourses look sickly.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dlr motors on and up, Eurobourses look sickly.

text.p: The dollar remained bullish in Europe on Tuesday, hitting new highs against the mark, yen and Swiss franc but bourses were nervous and mainly weaker following another overnight fall on Wall Street.
The dollar touched a 31-month high of 1.6565 marks and a 47-month peak of 120.78 yen and analysts said said it could surge higher if there was a strong showing in Tuesday's U.S. employment cost data.

"People are speculating perhaps we'll get strong data today and that's helping the dollar as well...as that could raise the chances of an early Fed rate hike," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.
By noon GMT, the U.S. currency was still a firm 1.6548 marks and 120.75 yen, well over a pfenning and a yen above late Monday European levels of 1.6413 marks and 119.43 yen.

"If we get the employment cost index reported above one percent, we will have good cause for concern and the market will take the dollar higher," said PaineWebber chief international economist Michael O'Hanlon.

A Reuters poll of economists showed the that U.S. cost employment index for the fourth quarter of 1996, due at 1330 GMT, was on average expected to rise 0.9 percent after a 0.6 percent increase previously.

The index was seen as key to any decision by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on interest rates at its meeting next week, especially after Fed chairman Alan Greenspan warned of risks of wage-driven inflation in his testimony to the U.S. Senate Budget Committee last week.
Meanwhile, analysts said the dollar was also helped by reports that neither Germany nor Japan appeared very worried about the dollar's strength against their currencies.
"They (Japanese authorities) don't see it as a major problem because they see it as a case of a strong dollar rather than a weak yen," Rayner said.
The dollar also touched a 33-month high of 1.4370 Swiss francs. It had retreated to 1.4345 by noon GMT but was still well above Monday's late European level of 1.4240.
The Swiss franc was unsettled overnight by a media report that Swiss Finance Minister Kaspar Villiger had said he was "relieved" at the currency's recent decline.
On the bourses, leading London shares were a quarter of a percentage point weaker after U.S. blue chips again slid overnight, by 35 points, following their near 60-point setback on Friday.

Investors continued to fret over Wall Street and dealers said they feared the Dow, which has lost nearly 200 points over the past three sessions after setting 10 record highs in the first few weeks of 1997, could be on the verge of a more substantial fall.
"Some people are starting to talk about the Dow dropping around 10 to 15 percent," one senior dealer said.
Equity traders said they would be watching the U.S. data just as closely as the currency market.

"Today's U.S. Q4 employment cost index is one of the most important economic releases of the week, if not the year if it marks a possible turning point in Fed monetary policy," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered in his daily outlook on Tuesday.

German shares also slipped, pulled down by the softer Wall Street, and the blue chip DAX index was down, though not by much, at midday. It was partially supported by the strength of the dollar, which is positive for German exports.

The Paris bourse was the exception, managing to move nearly half a percent into positive territory with the dollar's rise to more than 5.58 francs offsetting the negative effect of falling U.S. stocks and a bond market drop.
CURRENCIES AT 1205 GMT
The dollar was at 120.75 yen and 1.6548 marks compared with late Europe's Monday level of 119.43 yen and 1.6413 marks.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1205 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares had fallen 10.9 points to 4,201.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index gained 11.12 to 2,446.29.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 2.66 at 2,991.87.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed sharply higher at $357.25 compared with London's monday close of $354.60. Silver was stronger too, just above the $5.0 level.
